title: Feature Fragment Lab — lightweight composable response components
content:
Context / motivation:

Short: we want a lightweight abstraction that lets product teams compose small, reusable response pieces (fragments) at request time so we can: reduce repeated tokens across responses, speed up prototyping, and enable runtime wiring of small templates or micro-logic without shipping a full new model or prompt.

Background notes (brain dump):
- Many teams build similar scaffolding: small canned intros, privacy disclaimers, verification tokens, abbreviated user profile hooks, localized salutations. These are repeated across prompts and cost tokens.
- Current options: monolithic prompt templates per flow, server-side stitching of text, or expensive eval/rollouts to change behavior.
- Idea: a fragment registry + runtime composer. A fragment = small named snippet with metadata (tokens, placeholders, constraints, recommended model-compatibility, guardrails).

Goals / success signal (draft):
- First 90 days: ship a minimal fragment runtime that can be used by 2 internal teams.
- Metric: 5–15% reduction in median request tokens for targeted flows where fragments replace duplicated content.
- UX metric: < 2 developer-hours to create + wire a new fragment into an existing prompt (target).
- Safety: fragments must be linted for PII/assertions; block fragments that try to exfiltrate user data (proto policy).

Non-goals:
- Not a full templating engine. Not aiming at complex control flow (loops/conditionals) in V1.
- Not a replacement for model-first instruction changes. It's an engineering convenience and cost lever.

Surface sketch (V0):
- Registry: simple JSON store in config service with entries: id, display_name, short_description, body_template, placeholder_list, token_estimate, allowed_models, version, owner, tags.
- Runtime composer: at request time, caller can reference fragment ids and provide binding values; runtime expands fragments into a single prompt body using safe concatenation rules and optional separators.
- Admin UI (console): browse fragments, preview token usage, quick-insert into a route's prompt config.
- SDK change: small helper in JS/Python to resolve fragments when sending request. SDK can fetch and cache fragment metadata + body.

Example fragment record (V0 example):
- id: frag-salutation-compact-v1
- body_template: "Hi {first_name}, here's the short update:
"
- placeholders: ["first_name"]
- allowed_models: ["gptx-small","redwood-compact-1"]
- token_estimate: "~6"

Example runtime usage (pseudo):
- route prompt config: "prefixFragments": ["frag-salutation-compact-v1","frag-privacy-short-v1"], "mainPrompt": "User query: {query}
Action: produce summary"
- SDK resolves fragments (local cache -> registry), binds placeholders, concatenates with separators and produces final prompt to send to model.

User stories (initial):
- As a product engineer, I can create a fragment in the console with a preview so I can reuse standard phrasing across multiple routes.
- As a PM, I can add the "frag-support-sla" to the support route so all agents include the correct SLA wording without touching the main prompt.
- As SRE, I can see token impact per fragment on a per-route basis and roll back fragments easily.
- As an Eval engineer, I can tag fragments as testable and include them in regression suites.

Acceptance criteria (V0):
- CLI/console: create/edit fragment JSON, view token estimate, save version.
- SDK: fetch fragment metadata and bodies, local TTL cache, resolve bindings.
- Runtime: resolve up to N fragments and concatenate safely under route-level max prompt size.
- Security: validate fragment bodies against a small rule set (no raw key patterns, no full email addresses by default).

Experiment plan / rollout path:
- Phase A: internal pilot with 2 teams (console + dedicated route changes). Track token delta, error rates, dev time saved.
- Phase B: enable public feature flag for orgs on hosted API. Provide migration guide and best-practice examples.
- Phase C: expose fragments in Dedicated/Private with config sync tooling.

Metrics to collect (proposal):
- Primary: token-saved delta (tokens_before - tokens_after) aggregated by route and org.
- Secondary: fragment-usage-count, average fragment size, latency delta (should be negligible), fragment-failure-rate (resolve failures).
- Developer: time-to-first-fragment (from console open to route wired).

Open questions / risks (raw):
- How to handle fragment versioning and backwards-incompatible edits? Option: immutability by default, users create new version id (frag-foo-v2). Provide deprecation schedule.
- How to manage secrets/placeholders? Some placeholders might be sensitive (e.g., user_api_key). We need a policy: placeholders that map to secret slots are resolved server-side and never visible in console.
- Safety / prompt-injection: fragments introduce an additional attack surface (users could paste instructions that steer model). Need lint + optional sandboxed eval with a small adversarial prompt set.
- Model compatibility: certain fragments might exploit model capabilities (long/short). Provide recommended_model list and a per-fragment warning if used with incompatible model.
- Caching TTL: fragments cached at SDK will cause stale content—how to invalidate quickly? Consider CDN/long-cache + change webhook or versioned ids.

Implementation sketch (tech):
- Registry store: Postgres table + small Dynamo/Redis cache for resolution speeds.
- API: fragments.redwood.ai/v1/fragments/{id} -> returns body and metadata. TTL header + ETag support.
- Console: simple table + edit modal + preview pane (token estimate runs in the browser using a local tokenizer lib).
- SDK: small client-side resolver with fallback to server, support for offline mode if configured (embed small fragment set in repo).
- Runtime concat rules: normalize whitespace, ensure separator token "
---
" between fragments, apply prompt-length check, and abort early with structured error that indicates which fragment caused over-length.

UX edge-cases / heuristics:
- If a fragment binding is missing at runtime: optional modes -> (a) error; (b) insert placeholder fallback text; (c) drop fragment. Default to (a) during pilot, (b)/(c) as configurable.
- Fallback fragment: a special fragment that can be used when preferred fragment exceeds model size. For cost-safety, a "compact" variant recommended.

Short todo list (me):
- [ ] Sketch console UI mockups (Kai + me) — due 2025-02-18
- [ ] Prototype minimal registry API + simple SDK resolver for node/python (Samir) — due 2025-03-01
- [ ] Draft safety lint rules and tiny adversarial test corpus (Evelyn) — due 2025-02-25
- [ ] Wire telemetry events (fragment_resolve_start/end, fragment_cache_hit/miss) (SRE/obs) — due 2025-03-05
- [ ] Quick internal pilot README + sample fragments for Support and Onboarding flows — due 2025-03-10

Notes-to-self (random):
- Keep the initial model of fragments intentionally small: no logic beyond simple placeholders. If we get traction, extend to conditional blocks in V2.
- Think about discoverability: tags + suggested fragments show up when editing a route prompt.
- Could be interesting to surface per-fragment cost estimate in the Console billing view (preview incremental cost).

Links and inspiration (scratch):
- small-template libraries I've seen in other apps (internal link)
- related Redwood ideas: "snippet" and "prompt-components" notes (search drive)

Questions for next sync with Kai + Samir:
- agreement on versioning semantics (immutable ids or mutable with history?)
- pilot orgs: pick 2 internal teams that will benefit and are willing to instrument telemetry (Support, Onboarding?)

End of rough pad. This is intentionally informal — will convert to a short PRD and a one-pager if the pilot metrics look promising.
